page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n1 server family. It is configured with 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor using the x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading enabled. The system includes 360 GB of dedicated RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. It features an L3 cache size of 38 MB and supports hardware-level instructions such as AVX, AVX-512, AES, and FMA. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by bottom-tier results in stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core tests. However, the massive core count enables strong multi-core performance, placing it in the top tier for stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU extended instructions tests. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with read and write benchmarks for both small and large blocks ranking in the top 25%.

Given its high resource density and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, the n1-standard-96 offers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads that can leverage its 96 vCPUs and strong memory bandwidth. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, and database operations. However, it is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or workloads requiring local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
